clauses.reason: The clause revokes the designation of Unalaska, Alaska, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 31 (Alaska) and says that the order "shall become effective at the close of business January 15, 1941." The revocation is a one-time act with a stated effective moment, so the command was performed and ended at the close of business on January 15, 1941. The loss of port-of-entry status is a surviving effect of the completed act. No held instrument revokes, amends or restores the designation by executive order.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 8639 of January 14, 1941 (6 FR 455, Federal Register issue of Friday, January 17, 1941; FR Doc. 41-383, filed January 15, 1941) revokes the designation of Unalaska, Alaska, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 31 (Alaska), under section 1 of the Act of August 1, 1914 (38 Stat. 609, 623; 19 U.S.C. 2), and provides that the order "shall become effective at the close of business January 15, 1941." The revocation is a one-time act with a stated effective moment, so it was performed and the command exhausted at the close of business on January 15, 1941. Identity rests on the heading, the signing date of January 14, 1941, the Federal Register document line and the page; the machine-extracted text prints the closing order-number line with a stray character, which the packet records as a segmentation lead. The loss of port-of-entry status is a surviving effect of that executed act. The working text is the official Federal Register page text extracted from the PDF by OCR, not an authenticated transcription; page images were not inspected.

savings.reason: The designation of Unalaska as a customs port of entry was revoked effective at the close of business on January 15, 1941. The resulting absence of port-of-entry status is a surviving effect of the executed revocation, not a command that Executive Order 8639 continues to impose. The held text has no savings clause and no held source shows a pending right or duty under it.
